issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a 'Milkable' interface, but the solution repository introduces an interface named 'Dairy' (Dairy.java) and leaves Milkable.java empty. Classes that should implement 'Milkable' (Seal, Goat) instead implement 'Dairy' in the solution. This name mismatch between the specified interface and the solution implementation is a structural inconsistency that will confuse students about the expected interface name and which file to create/implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the interface name across artifacts. Rename the 'Dairy' interface to 'Milkable' (both file and type name) and have Seal and Goat implement 'Milkable'; remove the empty Milkable.java file. Alternatively, update the problem statement and UML to consistently use 'Dairy' instead of 'Milkable'. Ensure the interface file and type name match the name used in the specification.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to an interface named 'Milkable', and the template Main.java also references 'Milkable' in example usage. The solution implementation, however, provides an interface named 'Dairy' which is implemented by Goat and Seal (e.g., 'implements Dairy'), while there is no substantive 'Milkable' interface in the solution. This mismatch (Milkable vs Dairy) creates an unnecessary mapping burden: students expecting to implement or use 'Milkable' will find 'Dairy' in the solution and may be confused which name is correct.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent interface name across all artifacts. Rename the solution interface 'Dairy' to 'Milkable' and update implementing classes (Seal, Goat) to 'implements Milkable', or alternatively change the problem statement and template references from 'Milkable' to 'Dairy'. Prefer aligning the solution to the problem/UML by renaming 'Dairy' -> 'Milkable' to avoid student confusion.
